claims.text: The infant is at 37 weeks' gestation, which falls within the population eligible for risk stratification for early-onset sepsis. Acceptable approaches to this stratification include categorical algorithms using threshold values for intrapartum risk factors, multivariate risk assessment incorporating both intrapartum factors and infant examinations, or serial physical examination to detect clinical signs of illness.

Risk stratification relies on specific clinical risk factors whose occurrence, severity, and duration are used to assess EOS risk. Evidence supports the predictive value of gestational age, maternal intraamniotic infection, duration of rupture of membranes, maternal GBS colonization, administration of appropriate intrapartum antibiotic therapy, and the newborn's clinical condition.

Categorical risk factor assessment uses threshold values to identify infants at increased risk for EOS. One defined category includes a mother who is colonized with GBS and received inadequate intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis (IAP), with a duration of rupture of membranes >18 hours or birth before 37 weeks' gestation.

Another defined category in the categorical algorithm includes a mother who is colonized with GBS and received inadequate IAP but has no additional risk factors. This distinction is critical for determining the subsequent management pathway, as it differs from categories involving chorioamnionitis or ill-appearing infants.

Management recommendations based on the categorical algorithm include laboratory testing and empirical antibiotic therapy for infants in categories 1 and 2 (ill-appearing or chorioamnionitis), laboratory testing for category 3 (inadequate IAP with prolonged ROM or preterm birth), and observation in the hospital for ≥48 hours for category 4 (inadequate IAP with no additional risk factors).

Serial physical examination is an acceptable approach to detect the presence of clinical signs of illness after birth. This monitoring strategy may begin with a categorical or multivariate assessment to identify at-risk newborns who will then be subjected to serial monitoring, or it may be applied to all newborn infants.

packet.evaluation_question: A well-appearing infant has one confirmed maternal GBS risk factor. Explain risk stratification, examination and locally documented management options. Gestation 37 weeks; age 24 hours; setting neonatal unit.

evidence.text: A categorical risk factor assessment includes risk factor threshold values to identify infants who are at increased risk for EOS. Algorithms for the management of GBS-specific EOS have been used as a general framework for the prevention of all EOS. Risk factors used in such algorithms included (1) any

newborn infant who is ill appearing; (2) a mother with a clinical diagnosis of chorioamnionitis; (3) a mother who is colonized with GBS and who received inadequate IAP, with a duration of ROM being >18 hours or birth before 37 weeks’ gestation; or (4) a mother who is colonized with GBS who received inadequate IAP but with no additional risk factors. Recommendations in these algorithms include the following: laboratory testing and empirical antibiotic therapy for infants in categories 1 and 2, laboratory testing for category 3, and observation in the hospital for ≥48 hours for category 4.

The occurrence, severity, and duration of specific clinical risk factors can be used to assess the risk of EOS among term and late-preterm infants. Evidence has supported the predictive value of gestational age, maternal intraamniotic infection (represented either by intrapartum fever or the obstetric clinical diagnosis of chorioamnionitis), the duration of rupture of membranes (ROM), maternal GBS colonization, the administration of appropriate intrapartum antibiotic therapy, and the newborn clinical condition.

Infants born at ≥35 0/7 weeks’ gestation can be stratified by the level of risk for EOS. Acceptable approaches to risk stratification include the following: o categorical algorithms in which threshold values for intrapartum risk factors are used; o multivariate risk assessment based on both intrapartum risk factors and infant examinations. The Neonatal Early-Onset Sepsis Risk Calculator47 is an example of this approach; and o serial physical examination to detect the presence of clinical signs of illness after birth. This approach may begin with a categorical or multivariate assessment to identify newborn infants who are at risk and will be subjected to serial monitoring, or this may be applied to all newborn infants.
